scholarships.name: Bruce Campbell Memorial Police Foundations Bursary

criteria_texts: Bruce Campbell was an instructor at Algonquin College who was passionate about post-secondary education and creating opportunities for students in law enforcement. A former Sergeant Major with the Ontario Provincial Police (OPP) Auxiliary Unit, as well as an advocate for traffic safety, Bruce was diagnosed with esophageal cancer and his courageous battle ended in October 2019. Bruce will be remembered as an active community member who valued education, safety, and helping others. As a tribute to Bruce and his impact on all those around him, friends and colleagues of Bruce created the Bruce Campbell Police Foundations Bursary. In conjunction with this Bursary, the first annual Bruce Campbell Memorial Golf Tournament, will take place on September 21, 2020 at the Marshes Golf Club. The day will be dedicated to celebrating Bruce and raising funds for the Bursary.

scholarships.name: John Tattersall Bursary for Women in STEM

criteria_texts: To celebrate John Tattersall and his impact on Algonquin College, the John Tattersall Bursary was created in his honour, to help champion women in STEM (science, technology, engineering, and math). After a six-year career with the College, during two stints, the Executive Director of Facilities Management retired in August 2021. John joined Algonquin College in 2011 after a successful 36-year military career where he rose to the rank of Colonel, including command tours at home and abroad. Even if he didn’t attend the College as a student, John considered himself an alumnus since he learned everyday he came to work. In his work overseas, John witnessed how imperative education is to empowering a population as it is a key component to establishing equality in society. Awarded to female students in any STEM (science, technology, engineering, and math) program who can demonstrate financial need.

criteria_texts: Eight renewable awards, valued at up to $5,000 each per year, will be awarded annually to students entering Year One of any two-, three-, or four-year program, in any Faculty. Each year, fifty percent (half) of the bursaries will be allocated to students in a two-year diploma program. To be considered, students must be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or protected person as well as a resident of Ontario who has graduated from high school in the Ottawa, Perth, or Pembroke area in the last three years and pursuing their first post-secondary program. Selection will be based on a combination of demonstrated financial need, as determined by Algonquin College, as well as a reference letter from an individual who is aware of the student’s personal circumstances and can speak to their resilience in the face of adversity and potential for success in their post-secondary studies. Selected students must commit to working with a mentor throughout their studies. An application is required by March 31. This fund is made possible by a generous donation from The Joyce Family Foundation, which is committed to providing access to education for youth who face significant financial barriers and have demonstrated the ability to overcome obstacles and adversity.

intake_texts: THE STEPHEN LA SALLE AND JESSE BELL BURSARY FOR CULINARY MANAGEMENT STUDENTS | THE STEPHEN LA SALLE AND JESSE BELL BURSARY FOR CULINARY MANAGEMENT STUDENTS Background Algonquin College Culinary Arts alumni Stephen La Salle and Jesse Bell (Class of 2007–2008) are respected chefs, educators, and mentors within Ottawa’s culinary community. Both have taught at Algonquin College and are dedicated supporters of emerging culinary talent. Together, they founded Chef Appreciation Night, a monthly dinner series that showcases young Ottawa chefs while raising funds for local charities, with additional proceeds supporting this new student bursary. Stephen contributes his expertise in food preparation and nutrition to supporting people in need and is preparing to transition into a new career in full‑time teaching. Jesse serves as the Regional President of the Culinary Federation, where he promotes excellence across the culinary industry. Their shared commitment to community, mentorship, and philanthropy continues to elevate and inspire the next generation of culinary professionals. Criteria The Financial Aid and Students Awards Office will annually award a scholarship to a level 3 or higher, full-time, eligible student in demonstrated financial need who is registered full-time in Culinary Management program. scholarships.name: FOPLA Award for Diversity and Equity in Public Librarianship

criteria_texts: This award was created by the Friends of the Ottawa Public Library Association (FOPLA) to support racialized or Indigenous students to pursue their education and careers in an essential library sector, public libraries. The FOPLA Award for Diversity and Equity in Public Librarianship is given to a student who self-identifies as a member of a racialized or Indigenous community with a minimum GPA of 3.0 and enrolled in their first semester of the Library and Information Technician program. Eligibility Criteria: Applicants must be registered full-time Applicants must have a minimum of 3.0 grade point, average, Domestic (Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or protected person/convention refugee) students are encouraged to apply, Applicants must be enrolled in their first semester of the Library and Information Technician program offered at the Ottawa Campus. Instructions: Applicants must add their Social Insurance Number via their ACSIS account in order to be awarded funding. Applicants will be required to submit a 250-word essay. All applicants will be notified of a decision by email after the deadline. Application is available from October 1st to October 15th, 2023

application.instructions_text: https://www.algonquincollege.com/financial-aid/awards-bursaries-scholarships/fopla-award/

criteria_texts: The Brittaney Fraser-McCann Bursary was established in memory of Brittaney Fraser-McCann. Brittaney was a graduate of the two-year Practical Nursing program at the Pembroke Campus. She passed away on December 17th, 2021 after complications during her third endovascular coiling procedure to repair a brain aneurysm. She was 33. To honor Brittaney and her love of nursing and medical aesthetics, this bursary was created to support students as they strive to achieve their own nursing dream. The Bursary is awarded to one student enrolled in either the Practical Nursing or Bachelor of Science in Nursing Program in their second year who can demonstrate financial need. The Bursary is open to students enrolled at the Pembroke Campus, with first preference to a single parent.

criteria_texts: Diane Houston enjoyed a long and impactful career in Ottawa’s tourism sector, most recently serving as Director of Travel Trade at Ottawa Tourism. After dedicating her professional life to promoting the region and strengthening its visitor economy, she has now retired. Diane remains a passionate advocate for the tourism industry and is committed to supporting its future. Today, she helps students pursuing careers in tourism, events, sport, entertainment, and hospitality, encouraging them to develop the skills needed to enter these rewarding fields. Two awards of $2,000 each will be presented to Indigenous students (First Nations, Métis, or Inuit) enrolled in any of the Bachelor of Hospitality and Tourism Management, the Tourism – Travel Services, or the Bachelor Event, Sport and Entertainment Management programs who demonstrate the most passion and integrity for their studies.

criteria_texts: Schulich Builders: Scholarships for Skilled Trades Application Schulich Builders scholarships are awarded to students enrolling in full-time certificate and diploma programs within eligible skilled trade fields at participating Ontario colleges. Colleges offer the scholarships in programs with the most in-demand jobs in the skilled trade sector in Ontario. The program will award 120 scholarships annually with 10 scholarships available at each participating college. Scholarships are valued at up to $40,000 ($20,000 per academic year), supporting the costs of tuition, living expenses and tools. Schulich Builders will benefit from internal resources at the college to enhance their student experience and assist in their employment within their relevant field in the skilled trades upon graduation. Schulich Builders scholarships aims to recognize and enable Ontario’s future skilled trade workers, with an annual investment of over $3 million through top Ontario colleges.

Specifically, the student demonstrates the following: is cooperative, caring, pleasant, strives to build consensus and is always ready to lend a helping hand. Established by his family, the award is in loving memory of Blair H. Tetreault, who passed away in 2021. Blair graduated from the Broadcasting-Radio and Television Program of Algonquin College in 1981. Following work as an editor for various news and public affairs programs at the local Ottawa CTV affiliate, Blair transitioned to live sports broadcasting as an editor, tape operator, technical director, director and producer. He was a two-time Emmy Award winner. Blair was highly and warmly regarded for his technical expertise and collegiality.

He applied to Algonquin College for the scriptwriting program because he wanted to write comedies to bring happiness to everyone. He had a sense of humor no-one could match. When you were around Todd you couldn’t help laughing. People were drawn to Todd and when you met him you knew that you would not forget him. Todd brought people together with his sense of humor and creative mind. He brought his family and his school friends along with his hockey and college friends together. They have all remained friends to this day because of Todd. Always thinking of others Todd made sure others were looked after first. Todd lived life to the fullest even though it was a short one.

scholarships.name: The Builders' Lodge Masonic Bursary in Bachelor of Science in Nursing (Honours)

criteria_texts: Background: The Builders’ Lodge (No. 177) has been part of the Grand Lodge of Ancient Free and Accepted Masons in Canada within the Province of the Ontario for over 150 years. The Lodge was started by the builders of our Federal Parliament Buildings in 1865. We are the modern-day trustees of a rich heritage, and we believe that it’s important to give back to our communities in a positive way. In addition to the charity work the Lodge undertakes, it also provides bursaries to support students in Algonquin College’s Nursing programs. It is our hope that these bursaries will inspire deserving learners to pursue a path of service and contribute to building a stronger, more compassionate society.This year, the Lodge is pleased to offer a bursary to the Practical Nursing Ontario Diploma program and to extend its support to the Bachelor of Science in Nursing (Honours) degree program in recognition of Algonquin College’s celebration of 50 years of nursing excellence and the launch of the new four‑year program at both the Pembroke and Ottawa campuses. While the selection criteria for this scholarship do not require community involvement, the candidate should demonstrate a strong personal commitment to bettering their community through volunteer work undertaken outside of their program of study. Criteria: The Builders’ Lodge Masonic Bursary - Bachelor of Science in Nursing (Honours) will be awarded each year to a student(s) enrolled full-time in level 1 or level 2 of the Bachelor of Science in Nursing (Honours) program who demonstrate financial need and meet the academic requirements to continue in the program. The student(s) will receive $3,000. Not open to international students.

application.instructions_text: Apply through the bursary portal in ACSIS each term

unresolved_sections.name: Bursary Application
texts: Each term in the academic year, we open up our bursary portal for students to apply for additional funding. We use an almost all-in-one portal to help students apply. If you are unsure how to apply for a bursary, visit our How to Apply for Bursaries page to learn more. In order to be considered for many of the awards below you MUST fill out a bursary application when it’s open, so don’t snooze on this!
The Fall bursary application period is generally open from late August to late September.
The Winter bursary window is usually late December to mid-January.
The spring bursary application window will usually be late April to mid-May.
If you are looking for specific dates, you can check the Academic Calendar or the How to Apply for Bursaries page. In fact, you should really bookmark both of those; they are extremely handy.

Bruce Campbell Memorial Police Foundations Bursary

Bruce Campbell was an instructor at Algonquin College who was passionate about post-secondary education and creating opportunities for students in law enforcement. A former Sergeant Major with the Ontario Provincial Police (OPP) Auxiliary Unit, as well as an advocate for traffic safety, Bruce was diagnosed with esophageal cancer and his courageous battle ended in October 2019. Bruce will be remembered as an active community member who valued education, safety, and helping others. As a tribute to Bruce and his impact on all those around him, friends and colleagues of Bruce created the Bruce Campbell Police Foundations Bursary. In conjunction with this Bursary, the first annual Bruce Campbell Memorial Golf Tournament, will take place on September 21, 2020 at the Marshes Golf Club. The day will be dedicated to celebrating Bruce and raising funds for the Bursary.

Eight renewable awards, valued at up to $5,000 each per year, will be awarded annually to students entering Year One of any two-, three-, or four-year program, in any Faculty. Each year, fifty percent (half) of the bursaries will be allocated to students in a two-year diploma program. To be considered, students must be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or protected person as well as a resident of Ontario who has graduated from high school in the Ottawa, Perth, or Pembroke area in the last three years and pursuing their first post-secondary program. Selection will be based on a combination of demonstrated financial need, as determined by Algonquin College, as well as a reference letter from an individual who is aware of the student’s personal circumstances and can speak to their resilience in the face of adversity and potential for success in their post-secondary studies. Selected students must commit to working with a mentor throughout their studies. An application is required by March 31. This fund is made possible by a generous donation from The Joyce Family Foundation, which is committed to providing access to education for youth who face significant financial barriers and have demonstrated the ability to overcome obstacles and adversity.

This award was created by the Friends of the Ottawa Public Library Association (FOPLA) to support racialized or Indigenous students to pursue their education and careers in an essential library sector, public libraries. Eligibility Criteria: Applicants must be registered full-time Applicants must have a minimum of 3.0 grade point, average, Domestic (Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or protected person/convention refugee) students are encouraged to apply, Applicants must be enrolled in their first semester of the Library and Information Technician program offered at the Ottawa Campus. Instructions: Applicants must add their Social Insurance Number via their ACSIS account in order to be awarded funding. Applicants will be required to submit a 250-word essay. All applicants will be notified of a decision by email after the deadline. Application is available from October 1st to October 15th, 2023

Schulich Builders: Scholarships for Skilled Trades Application Schulich Builders scholarships are awarded to students enrolling in full-time certificate and diploma programs within eligible skilled trade fields at participating Ontario colleges. Colleges offer the scholarships in programs with the most in-demand jobs in the skilled trade sector in Ontario. The program will award 120 scholarships annually with 10 scholarships available at each participating college. Scholarships are valued at up to $40,000 ($20,000 per academic year), supporting the costs of tuition, living expenses and tools. Schulich Builders will benefit from internal resources at the college to enhance their student experience and assist in their employment within their relevant field in the skilled trades upon graduation. Schulich Builders scholarships aims to recognize and enable Ontario’s future skilled trade workers, with an annual investment of over $3 million through top Ontario colleges.

The Builders' Lodge Masonic Bursary in Bachelor of Science in Nursing (Honours)

Background: The Builders’ Lodge (No. 177) has been part of the Grand Lodge of Ancient Free and Accepted Masons in Canada within the Province of the Ontario for over 150 years. The Lodge was started by the builders of our Federal Parliament Buildings in 1865. We are the modern-day trustees of a rich heritage, and we believe that it’s important to give back to our communities in a positive way. In addition to the charity work the Lodge undertakes, it also provides bursaries to support students in Algonquin College’s Nursing programs. It is our hope that these bursaries will inspire deserving learners to pursue a path of service and contribute to building a stronger, more compassionate society.This year, the Lodge is pleased to offer a bursary to the Practical Nursing Ontario Diploma program and to extend its support to the Bachelor of Science in Nursing (Honours) degree program in recognition of Algonquin College’s celebration of 50 years of nursing excellence and the launch of the new four‑year program at both the Pembroke and Ottawa campuses. While the selection criteria for this scholarship do not require community involvement, the candidate should demonstrate a strong personal commitment to bettering their community through volunteer work undertaken outside of their program of study. Criteria: The Builders’ Lodge Masonic Bursary - Bachelor of Science in Nursing (Honours) will be awarded each year to a student(s) enrolled full-time in level 1 or level 2 of the Bachelor of Science in Nursing (Honours) program who demonstrate financial need and meet the academic requirements to continue in the program. The student(s) will receive $3,000. Not open to international students.
Apply through the bursary portal in ACSIS each term

positive: Eight renewable awards, valued at up to $5,000 each per year, will be awarded annually to students entering Year One of any two-, three-, or four-year program, in any Faculty. Each year, fifty percent (half) of the bursaries will be allocated to students in a two-year diploma program. To be considered, students must be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or protected person as well as a resident of Ontario who has graduated from high school in the Ottawa, Perth, or Pembroke area in the last three years and pursuing their first post-secondary program. Selection will be based on a combination of demonstrated financial need, as determined by Algonquin College, as well as a reference letter from an individual who is aware of the student’s personal circumstances and can speak to their resilience in the face of adversity and potential for success in their post-secondary studies. Selected students must commit to working with a mentor throughout their studies. An application is required by March 31. This fund is made possible by a generous donation from The Joyce Family Foundation, which is committed to providing access to education for youth who face significant financial barriers and have demonstrated the ability to overcome obstacles and adversity.
